scenes.text: On Venus, a single day lasts longer than an entire year.
Venus spins so slowly that one full turn takes about two hundred and forty three Earth days.
But it only needs about two hundred and twenty five days to go all the way around the Sun.
Venus spins backwards, so there the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.
Would you survive a day that long?

title: A day on Venus is longer than its year 🤯
caption: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once, but only about 225 days to orbit the Sun. And the Sun rises in the west there! Would you survive a day that long? 🪐
